title: Gradient saturation when discriminator is too strong
description: Early in learning, when G is poor, D rejects samples with high confidence, causing log(1-D(G(z))) to saturate and provide insufficient gradient for G.
canonical_description: adversarial training suffers from vanishing gradients when the discriminator confidently rejects generated samples

evidence.quote: Early in learning, when G is poor, D can reject samples with high confidence because they are clearly different from the training data. In this case, log(1-D(G(z))) saturates.
